An exhaustive eight-letter certificate over the complete eight four-letter adjacent-pair types has even-start and odd-start sets of 24 and 32 factors with no overlap. Repeated binary factors of length B+1 have starts congruent modulo dyadic B via parity and substitution synchronization; block identity A,C,A,complement(C),A proves uniqueness before 4B and repetition at 4B. Explicit n<=8 handles the base. Independent direct first-repeat enumeration n=1..256 and parity-certificate computation corroborate the all-n proof. Ratio extrema follow from dyadic plateau endpoints.
residual_risks: Finite prefix verification does not establish the unbounded dyadic formula; the substitution synchronization proof does.
